text:
Given two statements below :

Statement I : In $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ molecule the covalent radius is double of the atomic radius of chlorine.

Statement II : Radius of anionic species is always greater than their parent atomic radius.

Choose the most appropriate answer from options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a non-metal, the atomic radius is its covalent radius: half the distance between the nuclei of two atoms joined by a single bond. In $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$ the bond distance is 198 pm, so the covalent (atomic) radius of chlorine is 99 pm.

Thus it is the bond length that is double the atomic radius; the covalent radius equals the atomic radius, so Statement I is incorrect.

An anion has more electrons than its parent atom with the same nuclear charge. The extra electron–electron repulsion and the lower effective nuclear charge per electron expand the electron cloud, so an anion is always larger than its parent atom (for example, $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is 136 pm while F is 64 pm). Statement II is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: Which technique among the following, is most appropriate in separation of a mixture of $100\mathrm{mg}$ of $p$-nitrophenol and picric acid ?
options: 2-5 ft long column of silica gel
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
p-Nitrophenol and picric acid differ in polarity, so they can be separated by adsorption chromatography on silica gel.

The mixture is only 100 mg. For milligram quantities, preparative TLC is used: the mixture is applied as a band on a thick silica gel layer, the plate is developed, and each separated band is scraped off and extracted with a solvent.

A silica gel column 2–5 ft long is meant for gram-scale quantities, so it is not the most appropriate method for 100 mg.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Experimental reaction of $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}$ with aniline and anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$ does not give $o$ and $p$-methylaniline.

Reason (R): The $-\mathrm{NH}_{2}$ group of aniline becomes deactivating because of salt formation with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$ and hence yields $m$-methyl aniline as the product.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both A and R are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Aniline is a Lewis base. With anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$, the Lewis acid catalyst of the Friedel–Crafts reaction, the lone pair on nitrogen forms a salt:


[IMG]

Nitrogen acquires a positive charge, so the group becomes strongly deactivating and the catalyst is used up. Aniline therefore does not undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation, and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}$ with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$ gives no $o$- or $p$-methylaniline, so (A) is true.

The deactivated ring does not undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation at any position, so $m$-methylaniline is not formed either. (R) states that $m$-methylaniline is the product, so (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text:
Chlorophyll extracted from the crushed green leaves was dissolved in water to make $2\mathrm{L}$ solution of Mg of concentration $48\quad \mathrm{ppm}$. The number of atoms of $\mathrm{Mg}$ in this solution is $x\times 10^{20}$ atoms. The value of $x$ is $___________. ($Nearest Integer)

(Given : Atomic mass of $\mathrm{Mg}$ is $24\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1};\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}=6.02\times 10^{23}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $2\mathrm{L}\to 96\mathrm{mg}$ of $\mathrm{Mg}$

Number of atoms of $\mathrm{Mg}=\frac{96\times 10^{-3}}{24}\times \mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}$

$\begin{array}{l} =4\times 10^{-3}\times 6\times 10^{23} \\ =24\times 10^{20} \end{array}$

$x=24$

text:
$2.4\mathrm{g}$ coal is burnt in a bomb calorimeter in excess of oxygen at $298\mathrm{K}$ and $1\mathrm{atm}$ pressure. The temperature of the calorimeter rises from $298\mathrm{K}$ to $300\mathrm{K}$. The enthalpy change during the combustion of coal is $-x\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is $___________. ($Nearest Integer)

(Given : Heat capacity of bomb calorimeter $20.0\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$. Assume coal to be pure carbon)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Q}($ Heat evolved $)=-\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\text{system}}\Delta \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{n}}$

$\mathrm{n}_{\text{coal}}=\frac{2.4}{12}$

$\mathrm{Q}=\frac{-20(300-298)}{0.2}$

$Q=-200\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$

$x=200$

text:
When 800 mL of 0.5 M nitric acid is heated in a beaker, its volume is reduced to half and 11.5 g of nitric acid is evaporated. The molarity of the remaining nitric acid solution is x $\times$ $10^{-2} M. ($Nearest integer)

(Molar mass of nitric acid is 63 g mol$^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{m}$ moles of $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}=800\times 0.5$

Moles of $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}=400\times 10^{-3}=0.4\text{moles}$

Weight of $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}=0.4\times 63\mathrm{g}=25.2\mathrm{g}$

Remaining acid $=25.2-11.5=13.7\mathrm{g}$

$\begin{array}{ll} M & =\dfrac{13.7\times 1000}{400\times 63} \\ \quad =\dfrac{137}{252}=0.54 \\ \quad =54\times 10^{-2} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text:
At $298\mathrm{K}$, the equilibrium constant is $2\times 10^{15}$ for the reaction :

$\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})⇌\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})$

The equilibrium constant for the reaction

$\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})⇌\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})$

is $x\times 10^{-8}$. The value of $x$ is $_____________. ($Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})⇌\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})$

$k=2\times 10^{15}$

$\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})⇌\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})$

$\mathrm{K}^{'}=\frac{1}{(\mathrm{K})^{1/2}}=\frac{1}{\left (2\times 10^{15}\right )^{1/2}}$

$=2.23\times 10^{-8}$

$x\simeq 2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift
